basis: Manual PE/x86 and CIL control-flow review, JavaScript AST/value-flow review, extracted resources, and before/after scans. Scores and labels were not used as behavioral proof.
external_context: The supplied Triage and MalwareBazaar pages were inaccessible. No deployment authorization or original distribution provenance was supplied.

samples.identification: StormAttack resource DLL installer/injector, with a damaged embedded DLL
evidence: CRT entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0. Configuration at 0x404120 is 3, selecting 0x401900 (Active Setup installation), followed by 0x401390 (self-delete). Other configured branches implement service installation and DLL injection.

0x401900 derives a GUID name, obtains the current module path, builds an HKLM SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components subkey, and writes a REG_EXPAND_SZ StubPath at 0x401a4b. It reads the image with fopen/fread, patches a copy, writes it through fwrite, and calls CreateProcessA.

0x401260 opens LanmanServer\Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL at 0x401320 and replaces it at 0x40133e with a System32 DLL path. This is an alternate installation branch, not evidence every mechanism executes in this configuration.

0x401150 creates a selected host process, allocates/writes its DLL path using VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory, resolves LoadLibraryA through GetProcAddress, and passes that export as CreateRemoteThread entry at 0x40123d.
0x401390 obtains its own path, converts it to a short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del with output suppression, starts the cleanup process and resumes its thread.

Resource DLL/101 at RVA 0x5060 contains a 39936-byte PE. Its entry RVA 0x741a resolves to all-zero bytes; its declared import directory is also wiped. No executable flood implementation was recovered. Storm DDoS banners alone were not treated as proof of packet flooding.
samples.judgment: Self-installing DLL-injector code, service-DLL replacement, durable login activation and self-removal tip the balance toward malware. The damaged payload limits operation, not the intent supported by surviving installer code. Successful installation and runtime network effects were not demonstrated.
samples.traits: Retain the four accurate hostile findings; do not add ransomware, Remcos, or functioning DDoS claims from the collector filename or embedded banners.
samples.marker_line: StormAttack installer: DLL injection, Active Setup and self-delete

samples.identification: NanoCoreFinal-labeled custom .NET surveillance/RAT executable masquerading as Windows Update
evidence: Assembly entry token 0x06000033 is Program.Main at RVA 0x2910. It writes a Startup launcher and HKCU Run values, schedules itself on logon, tries an account-create/admin-add pair, performs the ms-settings DelegateExecute/fodhelper sequence, and starts hidden PowerShell commands disabling Defender protections.

Main invokes KeyloggerModule.Start (RVA 0x20cc), which installs hook type 13. HookCallback (0x21dc) records WM_KEYDOWN input with active-window titles into a StringBuilder; SendLoop (0x22e8) appends it to disk and calls SendToC2 with a Base64 KEYLOG record.

Main starts clipboard and screen worker delegates. The clipboard delegate (0x328c) reads clipboard handles and emits changed text; the screen delegate (0x33e0) calls CopyFromScreen, saves JPEG to a MemoryStream and constructs a SCREENSHOT record.

PasswordRecoveryModule worker 0x26ec builds Chrome and Edge Default profile paths for Login Data, Cookies and History, and calls SendFile. SendFile (0x37f0) reads bytes, Base64 encodes them and calls SendToC2. The stealer worker 0x352c also enumerates selected personal-file extensions recursively, sending files below 5 MiB.

Reverse-shell worker 0x38bc constructs a TcpClient, redirects a cmd.exe child, and starts two delegates (0x3844 and 0x3880) relaying socket input to child stdin and child stdout to the socket. HTTP task worker 0x3a24 reads /cmd response text, dispatches local-file requests or cmd /c execution, and forwards CMD_OUT records.
SendToC2 (0x3c78) UTF-8 encodes a record, XORs it with a repeating 32-byte key whose bytes are index XOR 0xaa, Base64 encodes it, URL-escapes it and builds an HTTP GET query.

Config initializer 0x2050 assigns C2_DOMAIN a full http:// URL. Callers prepend another http:// or pass the value directly as a TCP hostname. Thus the configured channels appear broken and successful exfiltration is not established.

Webcam code sends message 0x425, not WM_CAP_FILE_SAVEDIB (0x419); microphone code attempts to instantiate AxHost directly. TECHNIQUE:AMSI_Patch and ETW_Patch are only reporting labels. The six-byte injection buffer is not process hollowing. Those labels and broken capture attempts do not support additional successful-capture, AMSI/ETW patching, or hollowing findings.
samples.judgment: Covert input recording and file theft code combined with OS-product impersonation, persistence, Defender suppression and backdoor access outweigh the implementation defects. A sanctioned test harness could explain it, but no such provenance or authorization was supplied. NanoCore wording is a self-label, not independently established family attribution.
samples.traits: Retain accurate surveillance, credential-targeting, persistence and backdoor code findings. Move bare memory-protection flag references from allocation/modification into mem/protect/constant; stop PAGE_EXECUTE matching the longer PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE identifier.
samples.marker_line: Update RAT: keylogging and theft; relocate memory flag traits

samples.identification: WSH JScript Startup batch/PowerShell remote-script dropper
evidence: The large rec string, sonaraspadinha and repeated randomized variable assignments are unused. AST inspection shows no evaluator or decoder consumes them. Their alphabet compatibility and Unicode decoration were not treated as payload execution.

Executable tail creates WScript.Shell and FileSystemObject, resolves SpecialFolders(Startup), builds a .bat path, and passes the same built path to CreateTextFile. The returned writer receives a joined batch string.

The batch string starts PowerShell with WindowStyle Hidden and ExecutionPolicy Bypass, using IEX on Net.WebClient.DownloadString of an HTTPS URL ending in .png. The extension does not establish image bytes or steganography.

GetObject(winmgmts:...) -> Get(Win32_Process) -> Create receives the quoted batch path. The fallback WshShell.Run call is commented out. Therefore the file contains a WMI launch attempt, not an active WSH Run fallback.

WMI may reject direct batch-file process creation; the written Startup batch independently supplies later login activation. The downloaded stage was not fetched or executed, so its payload family and effects remain unknown.
samples.judgment: A persistent, hidden remote evaluator with policy bypass and no presented user-facing purpose is likely malicious. The verdict rests on the actual write/activation chain, not unused obfuscation-looking padding or reputation.
samples.traits: Require Startup-derived file creation, bound batch-path creation, a writer consuming the joined cradle, and actual WMI Create calls. Place the payload activation under execution/payload/script-eval. Remove comment/string-derived Run findings. Neutral file creation remains notable.
samples.marker_line: WSH dropper: hidden Startup downloader; bind write/WMI detections

placement_review.memory_flags: Exact references moved; allocation-protection selector retains its former execute-flag member explicitly. The execute-only matcher was separately tightened to a word boundary.
placement_review.run_observations: Preserve VBS/HTML textual spellings and use structured JavaScript call records. Generic compatibility composites may be omitted from rendered output, while their concrete atoms and consumer matches remain.
placement_review.budget_review: No directory limit was raised or new implementation partition introduced. Existing bare command tokens, source identifier references, AutoIt command text and hidden-window observations were moved to their supported subjects, with exact consumers updated.
placement_review.ancestor_selectors: The affected exec selectors were reviewed. The AutoIt matcher establishes command syntax rather than a process call, so it intentionally no longer qualifies through a generic process-creation directory; its two explicit MSI consumers retain it. Other old dispatch/flags directory selectors were absent. The memory-modification selector retains its moved member explicitly.
